resolutions.researcher_notes: OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', p.75 (verified live at the current opec.org URL; url_verifier flags it FAIL only because it's a compressed-stream PDF the substring screen can't read as text — I downloaded it and ran pdftotext manually, confirming the exact row 'Km-81.5/Brega  Sirte Oil  82  30  8,496,177  na' under the Libya heading; Wayback backup at http://web.archive.org/web/20260405233945/https://www.opec.org/assets/assetdb/asb-2012.pdf). The word 'operating' isn't literal in either source — status is inferred: OPEC lists it as an active, capacity-bearing line in the official gas-pipeline inventory, and the 2026 Libya Observer article confirms the broader Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company pipeline network at Brega (explicitly naming a nearby km-91 connection point in that same network) is currently live and being actively expanded/integrated. No source found reporting this specific segment shut in, damaged, or decommissioned.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 is titled 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' and lists Km-81.5/Brega under that table (confirmed via pdftotext, see Status notes for the exact row and the live/Wayback URL pair). Independently, the 2026 Pipeline Technology Journal article on the adjacent Farigh-Brega tie-in describes gas (not oil/products) flowing through this same Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company network into Brega.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10, p.75, row 'Km-81.5/Brega  Sirte Oil  82 [mi]  30 [in]  8,496,177 [1,000 scm/yr]  na'. 8,496,177 thousand scm/yr = 8.496 bcm/yr, matching GEM's 8.50 bcm/y to two significant figures. url_verifier reports FAIL on both the live and Wayback copies because it can't read text inside the compressed PDF stream — I confirmed the row manually with pdftotext (both URLs return the identical scanned bulletin, 200 OK). Only one underlying document found with this precise figure; no second, independent capacity figure located for this specific milepost segment (as opposed to the network as a whole), so tier is medium/single-source despite two access points to it.

Same OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 row: Length column is in miles (table header confirmed via pdftotext: 'Length (miles) / Diameter (inches) / Capacity (1,000 scm/yr)'), value 82 mi = 131.97 km, rounding to GEM's 132.00 km exactly. Single-source figure (live + Wayback copies of the same document); no independent second length figure found for this specific segment.
Same OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 row: Diameter = 30 inches, matching GEM's 30.00 in exactly. Single-source (live + Wayback copies of the same document).

OPEC ASB 2012 lists the Km-81.5/Brega line under the 'Libya' country heading in Table 4.10 (confirmed via pdftotext). Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article independently places the company's Sirte Basin fields and the Brega hub within Libya. Both endpoints (start/end) are within Libya, consistent with GEM's Start/EndCountryOrArea = Libya.

OPEC ASB 2012 names 'Sirte Oil' (Sirte Oil Company) as the owner/operator of record for this exact segment, not 'Libyan National Oil Corp' by name. Two independent sources corroborate that Sirte Oil Company is itself a wholly state-owned subsidiary of Libya's National Oil Corporation: Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article describes it as 'operating under the state-owned National Oil Corporation (NOC)', and an Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada research document (via ecoi.net) states multiple sources describe SOC as 'either state-owned, or a subsidiary of the state-owned National Oil Corporation (NOC)'. Neither source states an exact '100%' equity figure, so GEM's Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp/100% is a reasonable but indirect attribution (operator-of-record -> parent state company), not a direct name-and-percentage match — flagging this chain rather than treating it as a literal confirmation. Tier set to medium accordingly.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (p.75, Libya) lists the Sirte Oil Company gathering network as SIX distinct milepost-to-milepost segments, each with its own length/diameter/capacity, not one aggregated line: Attahaddy/km-91.5 (25mi, 30in, 28,320,589); Km-81.5/Brega [= P1868] (82mi, 30in, 8,496,177); Raguba/km-110 (88mi, 20in, 3,964,882); Intesar/Sahel (80mi, 30in, 19,824,412); Sahel/km-81.5 (49mi, 30in, 19,541,206); Km-91.5/Brega (92mi, 36in, 21,240,442) — all attributed to 'Sirte Oil' as owner/operator, all reported in units of 1,000 scm/yr capacity. No source found (OPEC or otherwise) that describes this network as a single pipeline/line rather than a chain of discrete named segments. The official statistical source itself treats Km-81.5/Brega as a standalone segment with unique specs distinct from the other five (different length, and Sahel/km-81.5 and Km-91.5/Brega in particular have different endpoints and different capacity/diameter than Km-81.5/Brega despite sharing the 'km-81.5' or 'Brega' token), which supports these being genuine separate segments of one connected gathering trunk rather than double-counted duplicates of the same physical pipe. No evidence found either way of GEM having mis-split a single segment into two rows; based on available sources, no redundancy is indicated for P1868 specifically.
